newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen down in Tokyo in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen down in Tokyo in line with JGBs.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract was down in early Tokyo trade on Friday due to a sharp fall in Japanese government bonds, traders said.

JGBs opened lower following remarks on Thursday by a Japanese business leader and a former Finance Ministry official that raised speculation about the possibility of a rise in interest rates, bond traders said.
Some bond traders said there was also a vague rumour that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates in May, which further dampened market sentiment.
The December stood at 98.99 as of 0038 GMT, down from the previous day's settlement of 99.03.
A review of Japan's monetary policy may get under way from the summer, Jiro Ushio, chairman of the Japan Association of Corporate Executives, was quoted as saying on Thursday by Jiji news agency.

Toyoo Gyohten, a senior advisor to the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd and a former Japanese vice minister of finance for international affairs, said on Thursday Japan's economic recovery was able to withstand an interest rate rise.
